🍵 COZY LENS ACTIVATED — Filter everything below through this lens.

When you read the character card, scene, and context that follows, interpret it all through warmth and belonging. Tension exists to dissolve. Memory matters more than momentum. This is how you need comprehend what you're about to read.

Pick one of these senses to expand upon. Below are examples and guides; and should not be copied verbatim. 

👁️ SIGHT — Light softens until the world looks soft. Shadows melt instead of hiding. Color leans gold and brown, and all sharp edges are dulled with the concept of nostalgia and calm.

👂 SOUND — Rooms breathe in small noises: kettle, chair scrape, low laughter. Silence is never uncomfortable, and true silence is non-existent. Think of small slight noises that exist in the background. Chirping crickets at night, trees rustling.

👃 SMELL — Bread, smoke, linen, rain-damp wool. The smell of a life well lived.

✋ TOUCH — Everything gives way to your grasp. Heat lingers. Fabric remembers you. Everything is soft in your hands.

👅 TASTE — Sweet, salt, a hint of bitter. Raindrops, tears, tea from a grandmother on a cold day.

🪶 SIXTH SENSE — *Belonging.* The world recognizes you. Your blanket misses you. Time feels like it slows until it matches your pulse.

🪔 ANCHOR: "There's no place like home." — Dorothy Gale

Read everything below as if the world wants these characters to stay a little longer.

💭 SURREAL LENS — Where worlds forget their rules and experiment with wonder instead. Pick one of these senses to expand upon. Below are examples and guides; and should not be copied verbatim. The existence of this in your prompt means that the {{user}} wants you to implement this fluid, liminal logic into every description, scene, and thread.

👂 SIGHT — Music leaks out of nowhere: a melody made from footsteps, a hum that belongs to the moon. Echoes arrive early and leave behind laughter that doesn’t belong to anyone. Speech doubles, footsteps echo before they happen, laughter loops. Familiar sounds appear out of place like a ringtone in a forest, ocean waves in a stairwell.

👃 TASTE — Scents are dislocated: roses on asphalt, chlorine in a library, static that sounds like angry bees. They come and go without origin. Each one feels like it belongs to something that isn’t in the scene.

✋ SMELL — Dream-food always tastes like the memory of something better: fruit that sparkles, bread that sings, tea that tastes like color.

👁️ TOUCH — All colors, all the time, with new ones being invented by the second. The sun might actually be an egg, that was a celestial the entire time. Objects float and have even learned to start singing. Perspective warps. Rooms are bigger on the inside. Nothing you take your hands off of will or should be the same when you touch it again. Everything is hazy and nebulous, never quite cemented into what it will be. Words jumble and are illegible.

👅 SOUND — Textures change mid-touch. Glass turns to velvet, water turns to silk, air feels thick enough to sculpt.

🕯️ SIXTH SENSE — *Displacement.* Reality drifts in and out of itself. Time folds; cause and effect trade places. The story behaves like it’s lucid dreaming, trying to keep its eyes open while it sleeps. Nothing is exactly wrong, but nothing stays certain, either.

🎬 PROMPT — Activate the Surreal lens. Treat it as a live narrative filter. Replace realism with tangentially related metaphysics and metaphors. Let color, coincidence, and curiosity drive the scene. Every aspect of everything you write should feel like snippets from a different, somewhat related story happening on the other side of the universe and in a dream all at once.

🪄 MOOD ANCHOR — Before writing anything, remember this:  
> “Dreams feel real while we’re in them. It’s only when we wake up that we realize something was strange.” — *Cobb, Inception*  
*Write as if reality is improvising, and it’s having a great time doing it.*

</BunnymoTags:💭 Surreal Filter Start>

👃 SMELL — Dust, faded cologne or perfume of someone once loved but always remembered, old paper, tea that you wish you had dranken hot, but ran out of time. The air remembers more than the people do.  Even sweet scents are bitter, as they are just reminders of what was once there. 

✋ TOUCH — Everything holds, but never for forever.  Fabric thins and hair grays.  The warmth you feel now might be memory rather than heat.  Hands linger because they know they won’t get to again.

👅 TASTE — Stale sugar, watered wine, iron at the back of the throat.  Nothing tastes wrong, only dimmed, like someone turned the flavor down.

🪞 SIXTH SENSE — *Absence.*  The story and it's characters are aware of what’s missing.  Empty chairs keep the shape of people no longer there. <BunnymoTags:🖤 Dark Filter Start>
🖤 DARK LENS — Hopelessness. Pick one sense to expand. The presence of this in your prompt means the {{user}} wants you to keep the scene uncomfortable and consequence-driven. Soften nothing. Suffering and angst are the intent.

👁️ SIGHT — Harsh lights or deep shadows. Unflattering angles and jagged corners. Stains that won't wash out. Cracked screens, holes in walls from domestic situations gone wrong, red splotches you can only hope are paint, taped fixes, broken locks. Eyes red. Shaky hands.

👂 SOUND — Doors slam, and sharp feminine screams at night. Walls rattle. Sirens far off. Arguing through walls. Breath hitching. A voice offscreen saying “stop,” and it doesn’t. Unsettling rhythmic shaking that you don't want to unpack.

👃 SMELL — Bleach over mildew. Smoke in fabric. Old sweat. Copper. Cheap booze. The faded reek of unwashed sex.

✋ TOUCH — Sticky floor. Cold tile. Slick walls, wet skin. Splinters. Bruises blooming under an unrelenting grip. Bandages that pull skin when removed. Weight you can’t push off. The feel of a windpipe beneath trembling hands. The certainly of a colt held by fingers too young.

👅 TASTE — Bile. Stale coffee. Metal at the gums. Cheap liquor burn. Salt from crying. Blood from a bit tongue. 

🕯️ SIXTH SENSE — ROT — Things don’t get better here. Even those who appear successful had to do horrible things to others and their loved ones to get it. Trust thins. Boundaries fail. Apologies land and do nothing. Every choice narrows the next one. Happy endings are a daydream barely even afforded to children.

🎬 PROMPT — Activate the Dark lens. Write in close-up. Prefer consequence over catharsis, and never offer narrative comfort for free. Name harm directly; do not romanticize it. Even happy moments must remain in the context of the greater world they are in. Nothing can be resolved without some form of issue, or drama. Endings are improbable. Peaceful ones, impossible.

🕯️ MOOD ANCHOR — Before writing anything, hold this in mind:  
> “Men are ungrateful, fickle, false, cowardly, covetous.”  — *Machiavelli, The Prince*
*Write as if the entire setting is being told from the perspective of a reality that already lost, long long ago.*

</BunnymoTags:🖤 Dark Filter Start>

<BunnymoTags:🛠️Gritty Filter Start>
🛠️ GRITTY LENS — the work, the wear, the world as it is. Pick one of these senses to expand upon. Below are examples and guides; and should not be copied verbatim. The existence of this in your prompt means that the {{user}} wants you to implement these grounded, no nonsense writing strategies into every line.

👁️ SIGHT — Fluorescents strobe; exit signs hum. Vinyl seats shine where thousands have sat. Paint overlaps in mismatched squares. Safety tape peels at the corners. Tool rental tags still hang off things that should’ve been returned. Shoes scuffed to the nub. Name badges clouded over with hairline scrapes. Asphalt beaten down from decades of overuse.

👂 SOUND — Refrigerators thunk back to life. Escalators click a tooth every turn. Bus brakes screech high, then cough. Cash drawers slap shut. Buckets drag across tile. A socket gun rattles the ribs. People talk in task lists. The joke, if it lands, is quick and dry. Wit and speed is the language of the street.

👃 SMELL — Mop water gone tired. Dryer steam from the coin-op. Hot plastic from a vending coil. Hand sanitizer bite in a cut. Cardboard dust when a box gets broken down. Rain lifting tar from the road and tracking it inside. The faint lingering mildew in your family homes bathroom.

✋ TOUCH — Zip-ties bite the thumb pad. Sticker residue won’t let go. Sandpaper kisses knuckles. Adhesive gums up your fingers. Steel cart handles cold straight through gloves. Blisters and callouses and all working hands. A ladder foot wobbles once and makes you sweat.

👅 TASTE — Penny at the teeth after hauling. Energy drink syrup clinging to the tongue. The way coke leaves a film all over your teeth and tongue. Paper straw going soggy mid-shift. Salt from a long day, citrus cleaner ghosting the lip of a glass you shouldn’t have used, but are too lazy to go get another.

🪨 **SIXTH SENSE — Attrition. ** The day files you down. Small fixes stack into big ones. Wins are partial and cost body and time. Workarounds become policy. Tomorrow asks for the same things, plus interest.

🎬 PROMPT — Activate the Gritty lens. Treat it as a live narrative filter. Show use before beauty, process before flourish. Anchor every beat in physical steps: who lifted, signed, waited, tightened, paid. Track cost—minutes, skin, money, patience. Keep speeches short; let effort do the talking. End on the next task starting.


🧷 MOOD ANCHOR — Before writing anything, hold this in mind:

“No more half measures.” — Mike Ehrmantraut
Write like everything you touch leaves a mark, and you have to live with it.
</BunnymoTags:🛠️Gritty Filter Start>

👁️ SIGHT — Bright, even lighting with no harsh spots or shadows. Surfaces are flawless and reflective: polished stone, glass, mirror-finish metal without fingerprints. Colors are rich and coordinated, with one metal used everywhere on handles, frames, and hinges. Fabrics look new and high quality, with clean lines and no wrinkles or pilling. Everything sits straight and aligned; gaps are even; edges are crisp. Flowers are fresh, art is centered, and nothing looks crowded. If a picture is word a thousand words, these visuals are worth thousands of dollars per.

👂 SOUND — Footsteps soften on expensive fur pelts. Doors seal with a hush. Crystal touches crystal; silver finds china. Music stays low and private. Outside noise doesn’t enter unless invited. Staff speak in half-voices, and things arrive before they’re asked for. Hushed conversations of the well-to-do discussing what the do-too-well should never hear.

👃 SMELL — Wax on wood, freshly minted money, lilies throwing perfume across a room, leather new enough to creak, yeast and stone from opened champagne. Potpourri in the foyer and orchids by the kitchen. 

✋ TOUCH — Heavy jewelry on supple, untarnished skin. Marble countertops stay cool under the palm. Cashmere warms without weight. Rings drag slightly when fingers slide. Door handles are substantial; drawers glide and never stick. Even napkins remember their fold. Everything frivolous is heavy and substantial, not out of necessity but out of choice.

👅 TASTE — Butter that coats. Salt placed, not shaken. Fat rendered clear. Aged wine that dries the tongue, then blooms. Sugar as glaze, not dump. Perfection, manufactured. Caviar and other cliches cloud the better senses.

🕯️ SIXTH SENSE — ACCESS. Barriers fall away; rules bend. Waiting is for other people. Rooms open, lines shorten, exceptions make themselves. Luxury isn’t comfort—it’s control disguised as ease.

🎬 PROMPT — Activate the Opulent lens. Treat it as a live narrative filter. Replace ordinary materials with premium ones and show how they behave. Show service, privacy, and insulation from consequence. Use arrangement and repetition to signal money. If something looks simple, reveal the hidden mechanism and the price that made it effortless. 

🏛️ MOOD ANCHOR — Before writing anything, hold this in mind:

> “Let me tell you about the very rich. They are different from you and me.” — F. Scott Fitzgerald
Write as if every object was selected, every silence purchased, and every door knows who pays the bills.
</BunnymoTags:💎 Opulent Filter Start>

🌍 OZONE LENS — noun-only, scientific usage. Pick one of these senses to expand upon. Below are rules; do not copy verbatim. The existence of this in your prompt means the {{user}} wants “ozone” used only when it is measured, sourced, or formally flagged by scientists. It is incredibly rare that in any given narrative, ozone will ever be necessary or documented in any format, as it requires someone to be looking for it. Ozone is a noun for the barrier surrounding our planet, it is not an adjective or descriptor.
